RCMP INVESTIGATING BREAK AND ENTER, ATV THEFT IN STEPHENVILLE CROSSING
(Nov 23rd)
Bay St. George RCMP is investigating an overnight break and enter at a residence in Stephenville Crossing, where an all-terrain vehicle was stolen.
Shortly after 6:30 a.m. on November 22, police responded to a report of a break and enter at a residence on Hillview Avenue.
Upon arrival, officers learned that the suspect or suspects had forced entry into the building and stolen a 2017 Kawasaki Mule side-by-side bearing Newfoundland and Labrador licence plate VGX 837.
Police are asking anyone with information, including witnesses or individuals with surveillance or dash camera footage from the area around the time of the incident, to contact the Bay St. George RCMP detachment as soon as possible.
Anyone with information is asked to call 709-643-2118 or contact their local police.

NL SCHOOLS TO OFFER CPR AND DEFIBRILLATOR TRAINING FOR STUDENTS
(Nov 23)
Students across Newfoundland and Labrador will soon have the opportunity to learn potentially lifesaving skills through a new partnership between the Provincial Government and Heart & Stroke.
The Department of Education and Early Childhood Development is introducing CardiacCrash, an interactive education program designed to teach students how to perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and use an automated external defibrillator (AED).
The program will be available to schools throughout the province later this month.
The program focuses on helping students:
- Recognize and respond to someone experiencing cardiac arrest.
- Understand how to perform CPR.
- Learn how to use an AED.
- Build confidence to take action during a medical emergency.
The initiative follows an earlier announcement to replace aging AEDs in schools throughout Newfoundland and Labrador.
Budget 2026 includes $500,000 to replace school AEDs and provide necessary training.
Education Minister Paul Dinn says the goal is to help students become more comfortable performing CPR and using an AED when needed.
The government is also working toward introducing a provincial AED registry to help improve access to lifesaving equipment.

NL GOVERNMENT INVESTING $1.2 MILLION TO BRING MORE FAMILY DOCTORS TO THE PROVINCE
(Nov 23)
The Government of Newfoundland and Labrador has announced a $1.2 million investment aimed at bringing more family doctors to communities across the province, particularly in rural areas.
The funding will expand the Practice Ready Assessment program (PRA-NL), delivered through Memorial University’s Faculty of Medicine, creating a new pathway for internationally trained family doctors to become licensed in Newfoundland and Labrador.
Qualified doctors who have already trained and practised medicine in other countries will undergo an intensive 12-week assessment to demonstrate they are ready to provide care in the province.
This allows eligible physicians to work toward obtaining a Newfoundland and Labrador medical licence without having to repeat their medical training.
Eight additional family doctors per year are expected through the new pathway with the existing assessment pathway continuing to accept internationally trained physicians. Together, both pathways are expected to bring at least 20 internationally trained doctors to the province each year. Recruitment efforts will place particular emphasis on improving access to family medicine in rural communities.
The province says it is working with Memorial University, the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Newfoundland and Labrador, and NL Health Services to support doctors through the licensing process and help them settle into local communities.
The investment is intended to address physician shortages and improve access to primary health care throughout Newfoundland and Labrador.

NL GOVERNMENT ANNOUNCES $1.55 MILLION FOR FOOD BANKS AS DEMAND CONTINUES TO RISE
(Nov 23)
The Government of Newfoundland and Labrador has announced $1.3 million in new funding for the Community Food Sharing Association, along with a final $250,000 contribution from the sale of American liquor.
The funding will help provide food to thousands of residents who rely on food banks across the province.
According to the province, the Community Food Sharing Association currently supports a network of 60 food banks serving more than 15,400 people each month, including:
- 4,700 children under the age of 18.
- 1,300 seniors.
- Thousands of other individuals and families experiencing food insecurity.
The number of people receiving assistance has increased by more than 40% since 2019.
The funding announced includes:
- $1.25 million in new provincial funding to purchase food.
- $50,000 to support the association’s operating costs.
- $250,000 as the final installment of the previously committed $1 million from the sale of American liquor.
The association says its purchasing partnerships allow it to obtain approximately $205 worth of food for every $10 received.
Based on that purchasing power, the $1.5 million allocated toward food purchases could provide the equivalent of more than $30 million worth of food for distribution throughout Newfoundland and Labrador.
The provincial government says the funding will help food banks respond to growing demand and distribute food to communities where it is needed most.

BAY DU NORD OIL PROJECT RECEIVES MAJOR APPROVAL - $6.4 BILLION IN PROJECTED REVENUE
(Nov 23)
The Bay du Nord offshore oil project has reached a major milestone after receiving development plan approval from both the provincial and federal governments.
Premier Tony Wakeham announced that both governments have approved the Canada-Newfoundland and Labrador Offshore Energy Regulator’s decision to permit the development of the project.
The approval brings Bay du Nord one step closer to a Final Investment Decision, expected in early 2027.
Led by Equinor Canada in partnership with Shell, Bay du Nord is expected to become the first deepwater oil development in Newfoundland and Labrador’s offshore area.
The project is located approximately 475 kilometres east of Newfoundland in the Flemish Pass Basin.
Key Figures:
- 400 million+ barrels of estimated recoverable oil.
- $6.4 billion in projected direct revenue over the project’s lifespan.
- 31 million+ person-hours of work projected over 25 years.
- Opportunities for local businesses, workers and contractors.
Premier Wakeham says the project could generate billions in future royalties, create employment opportunities and provide long-term economic benefits to the province.
Energy and Mines Minister Lloyd Parrott also highlighted the possibility of a provincial equity stake in the development.
Although the development plan has received government approval, the project has not yet received its Final Investment Decision.
Equinor and its partners must still make that decision before proceeding with development.
That decision is currently expected in early 2027.
If it moves forward, Bay du Nord would represent a significant expansion of Newfoundland and Labrador’s offshore oil industry.

TRUCK AND ATV SEIZED AFTER EIGHT ILLEGAL SALMON DISCOVERED
(Nov 23)
The provincial Resource Enforcement Division is continuing its efforts to combat illegal fishing and hunting on Newfoundland’s Great Northern Peninsula following several investigations.
On July 8, 2026, conservation officers from the Roddickton detachment responded to a complaint of suspicious activity near the Big East River.
During a joint patrol with Port Saunders RCMP, officers stopped a vehicle travelling on Rat Pond Resource Road.
An inspection of the truck and ATV uncovered eight untagged salmon, resulting in the arrest of both the driver and passenger for illegal possession of salmon.
Officers seized several items, including:
- A 2025 GMC truck
- A 2020 Can-Am ATV
- Eight untagged salmon
The investigation remains ongoing, with charges pending.
70 TROUT AND 15 SALMON SMOLT FOUND IN ILLEGAL NET
The following day, July 9, officers investigated reports of a fishing net in Bryants Raft Pond near Hawkes Bay.
Officers determined the net had been in the water for an extended period and removed it to prevent further fish from being caught.
The net contained 70 brook trout and 15 salmon smolt.
Other investigations on the Great Northern Peninsula this year have resulted in convictions for illegal possession of salmon, discharging firearms from a highway, hunting in the wrong area, and hunting within a posted commercial harvesting area.
Residents who witness suspected illegal fishing or hunting activity can report it anonymously by calling 1-877-820-0999.
The province says information from the public plays an important role in investigating illegal activity and protecting Newfoundland and Labrador’s wildlife resources.

HOME HEATING SUPPLEMENT INCREASED TO $1,000
(Nov 23)
The Government of Newfoundland and Labrador has begun issuing additional payments through the 2026 Home Heating Supplement Program for residents who use furnace or stove oil.
As part of recently announced affordability measures, the province has doubled the maximum supplement from $500 to $1,000 for eligible households.
Important info:
- Second payments began rolling out on Nov 20.
- Eligible residents who already applied do not need to reapply.
- Residents who have not yet applied can still submit an application if they meet the eligibility requirements.
- The application deadline is January 15, 2027.

BAY ROBERTS FOOD DRIVE COLLECTS SIX TRUCKLOADS OF FOOD
(Nov 23rd)
Bay Roberts Fire Rescue is thanking residents, local businesses and neighbouring fire departments following a successful annual Christmas food drive that collected more than six truckloads of food and nearly $2,000 in monetary donations.
In a social media post, Bay Roberts Fire Rescue said the annual food drive brought in $1,962.45 in monetary donations, along with more than six truckloads of food.
Firefighters were joined by mutual aid partners and members of the Spaniard’s Bay Fire Department, who dedicated their Saturday to helping with the collection.
The department also recognized the continued support of local grocery stores, including Foodland, Dominion and Powell’s Grocery, for their contributions to the annual initiative.
Bay Roberts Fire Rescue extended its thanks to everyone who donated, whether through monetary contributions, grocery donations or showing their support throughout the day.
A special acknowledgment was also given to The Helping Hand in Bay Roberts for its ongoing work supporting individuals and families in need throughout the communities.
The department said giving back to the communities it serves is just as important as being there during emergencies, adding that the success of the food drive reflects the generosity and community spirit of local residents.
Bay Roberts Fire Rescue.

NL WOMAN CELEBRATES REMARKABLE 111TH BIRTHDAY
(Nov 23rd)
A Clarke’s Beach woman celebrated a remarkable milestone over the weekend, marking her 111th birthday surrounded by family, friends, residents and staff.
In a social media post Sunday (Nov. 22nd), Harbour Main MHA Helen Conway Ottenheimer said she was excited to join in the celebrations honouring Mrs. Moores.
According to Ottenheimer, Mrs. Moores is believed to be the oldest person in Newfoundland and Labrador and the third-oldest person in Canada.
The Callingwood Downs Retirement Residence, where Mrs. Moores resides, also shared birthday wishes, describing her as someone whose kindness, stories and quiet strength have shaped those around her.
The celebration featured live music from Brycen Crowley and his band, Amper&And, who helped get the afternoon festivities and dance floor going.
Ottenheimer also shared a few details about Mrs. Moores’ food preferences, noting that she still enjoys a good feed of chicken wings and turkey necks, adding that she likes picking at the bones.
The retirement residence thanked residents, friends, family, staff and volunteers who helped make the occasion special.
Happy 111th birthday, Mrs. Moores!
Callingwood Downs Retirement Residence.

MAN FACING FIVE CHARGES AFTER THREATENING RNC OFFICERS
(Nov 23rd)
On early Monday morning (Nov 23rd), Shortly after midnight, Officers with the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) Operational Patrol Services responded to a residence in Mount Pearl following a report of trouble involving roommates. 
Upon arrival, while officers were speaking with the complainant outside the residence, the accused exited the home and began threatening officers. 
The 25-year-old male was arrested and charged with assault with a weapon, possession of a weapon for a dangerous purpose, mischief, uttering threats, and resisting arrest.

WOMAN CHARGED FOLLOWING DOMESTIC DISTURBANCE IN ST. JOHN’S
(Nov 22nd)
A 27-year-old woman is facing charges following a reported domestic disturbance at a residence in the east end of St. John’s.
At approximately 1:35 p.m. on Saturday, November 21st, members of the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) Operational Patrol Services responded to a residence following a report of a domestic disturbance in progress.
Officers spoke with the complainant, who advised that he had been assaulted by his ex-girlfriend.
Following further investigation, officers located the 27-year-old woman and placed her under arrest.
She was charged with assault and mischief and held for court in the morning.

PANHANDLER ACCUSED OF ASSAULTING MAN IN DOWNTOWN ST. JOHN’S
(Nov 22nd)
A 27-year-old woman is facing multiple charges following an assault at a business on Harvey Road in Downtown St. John’s.
At approximately 11:30 a.m. on Saturday, November 21st, members of the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) Operational Patrol Services responded to a business on Harvey Road following a report of an assault in progress.
Officers spoke with the complainant, who reported that a young female who was panhandling had asked him for spare change. When he advised that he had none, the female allegedly sprayed him with an unknown substance.
Officers located the 27-year-old woman walking in the area. She resisted officers during the arrest.
The woman was charged with assault with a weapon, resisting arrest and failure to comply with a probation order.

RETIRED METROBUS GIVEN NEW PURPOSE AS MOBILE COMMUNITY SUPPORT SERVICE
(Nov 21st)
A retired Metrobus is getting a new purpose in the community, as it has been transformed into a mobile ministry bus designed to support people experiencing homelessness and others in need.
According to the City of St. John’s, Metrobus donated a paratransit bus to the Anglican Diocese of Eastern Newfoundland and Labrador in June 2025.
Since the donation, approximately 60 volunteers and community partners have helped transform the vehicle into the Community Connector.
The mobile service will provide hot and cold beverages, light snacks, toiletries and clothing items to individuals experiencing homelessness and others in need. It will also help connect people with additional supports and services.
On Friday, Nov 20th, the Anglican Diocese officially received the keys to the bus. Volunteers are expected to begin working in the community over the next few weeks.
The City of St. John’s thanked everyone who helped give the retired bus a new purpose in the community.

ONE PERSON TAKEN INTO CUSTODY FOLLOWING POLICE OPERATION IN GAMBO
(Nov 21st)
The RCMP has concluded a police operation in Gambo Saturday morning, with one person taken into custody.
Around 6:15 a.m. on Saturday (Nov 21st), the RCMP issued a public advisory notifying residents of an increased police presence in the Norman’s Road area of Gambo due to an ongoing police operation.
Police advised there was no immediate threat to public safety but asked residents and travellers to avoid areas where officers were present to allow them to conduct their work.
Shortly after 6:30 a.m., the RCMP provided an update confirming the operation had concluded and one person had been taken into custody.
Residents and travellers were advised they could resume their regular activities in the area. However, an increased police presence will remain in the community as the investigation continues.
The RCMP thanked the public for their cooperation.
